## The full document lifecycle

Five API endpoints plus a visual Studio for building, testing, and deploying workflows. Supports 30+ file types.

Parse`/parse`Convert any document into structured JSON with text, tables, and figures. Layout-aware chunking optimized for LLMs.Extract`/extract`Define a JSON schema and pull specific fields from documents. Get exactly the data you need, nothing more.Classify`/classify`Route documents by type before processing. Define categories in natural language, no training data required.Split`/split`Divide documents into logical sections using natural language descriptions for targeted downstream processing.Edit`/edit`Fill PDF forms and modify DOCX files programmatically with natural language instructions.Studio Build, test, and deploy document workflows visually. Inspect results with bounding-box-level citations.

Install token  | The `rnpm_…` token in your `.npmrc`. It lets `npm install` download the packages
Reducto API key  | Your usual Reducto API key. Your server sends it with usage reports, so Reducto can bill them to your organization
License proxy  | A small route on your backend. A browser editor sends its license traffic there, and the route adds your API key. Your API key never goes to the browser
Session  | One document in use, for about 60 minutes from its first activity. This is what you pay for

Note

A Session here is a billing unit. It is not `DocxSession`, the editing type in the API reference.

## What you pay for

You pay once per Session. A Session starts when you open or create a document, in code or in an editor. Work on the same document in the next 60 minutes is part of that Session. If you save the file and open it again in those 60 minutes, on any machine, it stays in the same Session.

A compare or a combine of two documents counts as one Session.
